subject.title: [Feature]: sessions_kill should terminate all child exec processes spawned by a session

question: What public session-scoped process-control contract should OpenClaw expose for listing and terminating exec children spawned by a stored session?
rationale: The code has internal scoped process primitives, but exposing them through Gateway/RPC/CLI changes process visibility, termination authority, and session lifecycle semantics that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Add explicit session exec list/kill APIs
options.body: Introduce additive Gateway protocol and CLI commands that list and cancel exec children for a canonical session scope with explicit authorization and per-run results.

options.title: Extend existing abort/delete semantics
options.body: Make sessions.abort or sessions.delete optionally include process cleanup, preserving current defaults and documenting the stronger opt-in behavior.

options.title: Keep lower-level primitives only
options.body: Decline a public session-wide process-control surface and document that operators must use narrower process-tool or admin-specific controls.

recommendation.title: Add explicit session exec list/kill APIs
recommendation.body: Introduce additive Gateway protocol and CLI commands that list and cancel exec children for a canonical session scope with explicit authorization and per-run results.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent process supervisor and session-surface history makes this the strongest available routing owner for the API and lifecycle decision.
